subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for the active skill's intended host execution path while remaining stripped from unrelated generic exec children?
rationale: The reported behavior is source-backed and documented host-run env injection supports the expectation, but the repair changes how secrets cross into executable child processes and must be reconciled with the inverse leak issue.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly configured for the active skill to reach the intended skill-owned host execution path, with tests that dangerous host names stay blocked and unrelated generic exec loses skill secrets.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare each sensitive env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys are not expected to work.

options.title: Define a new credential contract
options.body: Defer the bypass and design a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential delivery path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly configured for the active skill to reach the intended skill-owned host execution path, with tests that dangerous host names stay blocked and unrelated generic exec loses skill secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest recent merged history in the overlapping skill env and SecretRef repair path.
